column1: #meta label(residence_tower) message(Dig a five floor residential tower in one pass. Place the cursor on the top floor where the central stair goes; the plan repeats down so every floor shares one stair shaft.)
tags: meta, multi-level, tower, repeat, starter

description: A #meta blueprint that stacks one floor into a five level residential tower. The meta references a single #dig blueprint by its label (/residence_floor) and applies the repeat(down 5) marker
column2: so the floor is stamped five times
column4: all sharing the central up/down stair (i). This is the corpus's first #meta example: a meta blueprint orchestrates other blueprints in the same file by label rather than painting tiles itself. A meta can list several /label references (one per line
column5: with #> or #< to step a Z-level between them) to chain multiple phases
column6: and each reference can carry its own shift() or transform() marker to offset
column8: or flip the blueprint it applies. Note the marker is written repeat(down 5) with no comma: inside a CSV cell a comma would split the reference into two columns
column9: and Quickfort treats the comma as optional. Run it with the cursor on the top floor stair tile and DFHack designates the whole shaft at once.
